description: Universal mail rules — domain-pattern-based, language-neutral (English), no profile identity. Safe to publish. Meant to be merged with a profile overlay at build time.
_folders_doc: Numeric 1*-9* folders are project-scoped, not sender-scoped -- that's what F0 (filters.views, axis=sender) is for. Logistics (flights/rideshare/postal/food-delivery) and Development (code hosting/SaaS dev tools/learning) were retired as numeric targets: covered by Fh Travel / Fe Dev-Tech in the sender axis instead. Only their housing-search subset survives, as 24 House. 30 CLOUD's GH-Workflows/Cloud-Reports/Rss-Notifications and VPS-Oracle/Google/Git live under `folder_groups` below (31/32 are two-level: a parent + 3 children each), not in this flat map.
_folders_ui_doc: Visual section-headers — flat sibling mailboxes (NOT actual parents) that alphabetically sort just before each numeric block (10_ before 11/12/..., 20_ before 21/..., etc). Maddy creates these via the legacy `folders_ui` schema (see flake.nix line 82) and Stalwart's jmap-sorter now mirrors them so the two engines have identical mailbox listings. They are not routing targets — no rule.copy_to references them.

inbox_copy.comment: Stalwart's fileinto :copy files a message into INBOX + its category folder as ONE JMAP object with ONE shared keywords set (mailboxes are labels, not IMAP folders) — verified live, not a Sieve ordering trick. There is no such thing as read-in-INBOX-but-unread-in-category for the same object here, so `enabled:true` (add \Seen after fileinto, banking on it only reaching the later implicit keep) marked BOTH read; every category folder measured unreadEmails=0. `enabled:false` embraces the shared flag instead of fighting it: a message is unread everywhere it's filed until it's actually read in any one of them, same as a Gmail label. Toggle back to true only if you want everything pre-read at delivery again (defeats unread counts everywhere, not just INBOX).

cleanup.comment: Used by cleanup-stale-mailboxes.sh, not by delivery filter.

folder_renames._doc: One-time in-place mailbox renames (old name -> new name) applied by jmap-sorter BEFORE ensure_mailboxes/cleanup, so a renamed folder KEEPS its emails (JMAP Mailbox/set name update) instead of being reaped + recreated empty. Idempotent, three cases: old absent -> no-op; old present and new absent -> in-place name update; old AND new both present -> MERGE (move every email from old into new, then destroy the emptied old). The merge case previously no-op'd, which stranded 230 messages in 'Aa 📬 Others (fallback)' once '91 📬 Others (fallback)' existed.

folder_options._doc: Per-folder client visibility, applied by jmap-sorter's ensure_mailboxes to EVERY folder it manages -- the numeric 1*-9* folders, folder_group children (Rss Notifications, GH Workflows, VPS *), the A*-F* filter views and the '_' section headers alike. One uniform mechanism, so an RSS folder is configured exactly like a mail folder.
folder_options._doc_subscribed: subscribed = the IMAP LSUB / JMAP isSubscribed bit: whether a client lists the folder in its normal folder menu at all. Stalwart CREATES mailboxes unsubscribed, which is why folders this engine made were missing from client menus -- measured on oci-mail, 53 of 60 were unsubscribed, i.e. everything except the 7 built-in system folders. Default true. Set an override to false to hide a folder from the menu WITHOUT deleting it or touching its contents.
folder_options._doc_notifications: There is deliberately NO per-folder 'notify me' toggle here. JMAP models no such mailbox property, so a setting for it in this file would silently do nothing -- the exact class of dead config this engine is written to avoid. Client notification behaviour follows subscription (above) plus the folder's special-use role, which are the real honoured knobs.
folder_options._doc_policy: Only the F* sender-axis folders are subscribed. Stalwart serves JMAP and IMAP from ONE mailbox store, so a folder cannot exist in JMAP but be absent from IMAP -- subscription is the only lever. Default false keeps the full 1*-9* + A*-E* structure intact server-side for JMAP/sorting while an IMAP client's folder menu shows just INBOX + F*.

filters._doc: Dynamic cross-cutting filter views maintained by jmap-sorter each poll over emails in the numeric 1*-9* folders. Multi-mailbox membership only (no copies, no $seen changes); add+remove each poll so time/read windows stay current.
filters._axis_doc: Each view declares its axis and whether it is volatile. A volatile view depends on wall-clock time or read state and must be re-evaluated every poll; a static view is a property of the message itself (size, attachments) and is computed once. The size axis is a PARTITION: its buckets are half-open [lo,hi) and must tile the whole range, so every message lands in exactly one. That invariant is what lets the sorter use size-view membership as the sentinel for 'static views already computed' -- guarded by 9_others/test/test_mail_filter_views_partition.sh.

views._doc: Any tag flag that already marks 'this matters': login/security alerts, money (invoices, receipts, subscriptions, insurance, bank mail), explicit review requests. Needs those specific rules' engines.stalwart flipped to full/tag_only (see rules[] below) -- they were all 'drop'/'route_only' before, so these flags were never emitted on Stalwart.
Everything that is neither Junk nor Important -- NOT(Ec) AND NOT(Ea), kept in sync by referencing the same two predicate trees rather than a third hand-written definition.
Same predicate as route.junk.spam_flagged.when, verbatim -- one spam signal, not two definitions of it to keep in sync.
DE/ES/EU/PT/US gov + tax authorities, plus tax.service.gov.uk and .gov.br from the existing route rules. No courts/legal domain known yet.

Recruiters only (career platforms + recruiter-subject detection). Employer/Clients/Coworkers need this account's real employer/client/coworker addresses -- none exist anywhere in this repo, so they're deliberately left out rather than guessed. Add them to this predicate's any_of when known.
Marketing/Promo has no sender domain of its own (mixed into every retailer's), so it's detected by subject instead, same values as tag.info.promo_en + tag.profile.promo_es_de.
Telecom/Energy/Housing/Health. No energy provider outside DE/ES known yet.

PLACEHOLDER -- always false (empty any_of). Generic ISP domains (gmail.com, gmx.de, web.de, outlook.com, icloud.com) are NOT classifiers, they're shared by millions of unrelated senders -- personal mail needs actual Family/Friends addresses, which live nowhere in this repo. Left empty on purpose rather than guessed; fill in any_of with real addresses/domains when available.
Fallback: matches nothing Fa-Fk already claims. References those same predicate trees (not a re-typed copy) so it can't silently drift out of sync when a domain is added above.

rules.comment: Route anything flagged by upstream spam engines (Stalwart internal, Gmail/Outlook via mail-puller, SA-style headers) into the unified Junk folder. Runs before all other routes so spam never pollutes category folders.

Folder 14 (cloud_workflows) was declared but unreachable — zero rules targeted it. GitHub Actions/CI notifications share github.com with ordinary GitHub mail, so route on the CI-specific signal (X-GitHub-Reason: ci_activity, or a 'Run failed:'/'workflow run' subject) rather than domain. Priority 95, BEFORE route.dev.code_hosting (100), so CI mail lands in 14 first and everything else still falls through to 31.
